# Architecture: Blog Website Application

## Overview
The blog application is a lightweight full-stack web app designed for a visitor-facing reading experience and an admin-focused publishing workflow. It follows a simple client-server architecture with a single Express server serving static frontend assets and a browser-based datastore using localStorage for persistence.

## Goals
- Let visitors browse a list of blog posts.
- Let admins create blog posts with title, content, and summary.
- Support AI-like summary generation through a deterministic content summarization function.
- Keep the implementation responsive and easy to run locally.

## Architecture summary

### 1. Frontend layer
- A single-page interface built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
- Blog list and details are rendered on the client for fast interaction.
- The admin panel includes a form for new blog creation and summary generation.

### 2. Application server
- Node.js + Express hosts the app and serves the static files.
- The server provides the root page and assets without database dependencies.

### 3. Persistence layer
- Browser localStorage stores blog records so the app retains data across refreshes.
- This is appropriate for a capstone project that prioritizes viability and demonstration over a backend database.

### 4. AI summary service
- The app contains a lightweight summary generator that extracts key language from the article body to simulate AI-assisted summarization.
- This satisfies the requirement for generating summaries and saving them with the blog entry.

## Component breakdown

### Public blog experience
- Displays all blog cards with title and excerpt.
- Opens detailed article content when selected.
- Renders a compact, responsive layout optimized for reading.

### Admin publishing flow
- Collects title and content from the admin.
- Generates a summary from the submitted text.
- Saves the article to localStorage and refreshes the blog list.

## Data model
A blog is represented as:
- id: unique identifier
- title: string
- content: string
- summary: string
- createdAt: ISO timestamp

## Security and validation
- Input fields are validated for empty values before saving.
- Content is sanitized for safe display in the DOM.
- The app avoids external API keys and keeps the demo self-contained.

## Performance considerations
- Static page delivery keeps initial load quick.
- The UI renders a small local dataset in-memory after reading from localStorage.
- CSS and JavaScript are intentionally lightweight for sub-3-second page-load targets.
